title: Semantic equivalence fuzzing harness to detect cache-hit-induced output divergence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a fuzzing-based evaluation harness that stresses the KV/prefix cache paths with semantically equivalent prompt perturbations to detect subtle output divergence caused by cache hits. The goal is to catch correctness regressions introduced by config changes (quantization, kernel swaps, prefetch heuristics) or model variants that only manifest when the cache path is exercised.
motivation: Recent incidents revealed low-rate but high-severity user-facing drift when KV cache reuse interacted with quantized kernels and a new prefetch heuristic. Unit tests and token-difference checks miss semantically equivalent shifts (rewording, paraphrase) that still change meaning. We need a continuous, automated way to surface semantic regressions tied to cache hits and gate rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness that generates N=100k cache-hit vs cache-miss pairs from production-like prompt distributions (configurable).
A battery of semantic-similarity checks (embedding distance, entailment classifier, label-preserving heuristics) and an aggregated divergence score with thresholds mapped to release gates.

Automated CI job that runs on PRs touching runtime cache code or model backends and fails when divergence score > threshold for any stratified cohort (customer templates, safety prompts, long-tail tokens).
Dashboard tile in Console showing per-commit delta, top offending prompts, and signal breakdown (token mismatches, semantic score, hallucination indicator).
Runbook entry that triages alerts into: revert, hotfix, or risk-accepted with mitigations (disable cache, route to fallbacks).
deliverables: fuzzer service producing canonical pairs and metadata (prompt, seed, prefix-length, hit-mask)
scorer library (embedding-based similarity + entailment checks + heuristics)
CI integration and pre-merge gate for runtime and model config PRs
Console dashboard and alerting rules linked to rollout pipeline
Runbook and incident template for cache-hit regressions
approach: 1) Create a corpus sampler seeded from anonymized production routing samples and synthetic prompt families (instructions, completions, chat turns). 2) For each sampled prompt, produce two executions: (a) warm run with synthetic prefix to force cache hit semantics, (b) cold run with cache bypassed. 3) Normalize outputs (strip ids, timestamps) and compute multiple signals: token-diff histogram, cosine distance of sentence embeddings, NLI-based entailment score, and a small classifier for hallucination-like patterns. 4) Aggregate across stratified cohorts and compute a weighted divergence metric. 5) Trigger CI/alert on cohorts exceeding configurable thresholds.
integration_plan: Hook the CI job into the runtime repo and model onboarding pipeline. Add a pre-deploy check for dedicated/private rollouts. Expose a lightweight API so other teams (model-op, console) can run targeted probes on demand. Backfill a 30-day baseline for dashboarding.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from paraphrase detection thresholds. Mitigation: tuned validation on labeled anchor set and manual curation loop.
Risk: Privacy concerns running production prompts in fuzzing. Mitigation: sampling and anonymization, enforcement of PII redaction before storage.
Risk: High compute cost for large-scale warm vs cold comparisons. Mitigation: stratified sampling, fast-path heuristics, and run only on commits that touch cache/model code by default.
runbook: If dashboard enters yellow/red: 1) run localized replay on top 100 offending prompts with full traces. 2) attach PR/commit hash, kernel/profile, quantization flags, and model variant. 3) if semantic divergence confirmed, follow rollout policy: immediate rollback for red in hosted API, schedule hotfix for dedicated/private if impact limited. 4) notify SRE/Model-Ops/PMs via #kv-fuzz-alerts channel.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal-only CI gating and daily dashboard (2 weeks). Phase 2: automated alerts wired to release pipeline and canary gating (4 weeks). Phase 3: integrate into runtime canary policies with automated fallback toggles (8 weeks).

notes: Avoid naming stable customers in stored artifacts. This harness is intended to complement, not replace, existing unit tests and token-level regression suites. Long-term goal: surface semantic regressions early enough to either rollback or route to a safe fallback model variant.
verification_steps: Run CI job on a branch that modifies a kernel selection flag and observe divergence metric change.
Manually review top 50 offending prompts and confirm semantic change using entailment classifier.
Validate false_positive_rate < 8% on the curated anchor set before enabling blocking gate.
